findings.observation: Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) shows adjacent properties with zoning designations clearly labeled. Vision tool analysis confirmed that SF-3 zoning is labeled to the west on Lot A, Subdivision of Lots No. 5, No. 7, and No. 8 of Wendlandt's Subdivision. Additional adjacent property zoning labels identified include: CS-V (commercial to east across S Lamar Blvd), CS-MU-V-CO (Sage Condominiums to south), CS and CS-V (properties to north), and P (apartment/condo and government services to west). Each property block includes zoning designation, lot/subdivision information, and current use. The CC Application Section 10 confirms the site is subject to Compatibility Standards (marked 'Yes'), and facts.md confirms adjacent SF-3 property (GeoID 0100050259) to the west triggers compatibility per LDC 25-2-1053.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires a land use map showing adjacent land uses when the site is subject to Compatibility Standards. The site IS subject to compatibility because it is zoned CS-V-DB90 and CS-V-CO (more intense than MF-4) AND is within 75 feet of an SF-3 triggering property to the west. Sheet 13 serves as the required land use map by comprehensively showing adjacent properties with their zoning designations, lot information, and current uses labeled around the entire site perimeter. The SF-3 triggering property is clearly identified, satisfying the completeness requirement to show adjacent land uses for compatibility review. Sheet 13 is the appropriate sheet for this purpose as it shows the overall site context.
findings.explanation: Sheet 13 provides land use map showing adjacent property zoning labels including SF-3 residential to west

findings.observation: Sheets 35 and 36 provide building elevations for all four building faces. Sheet 35 shows North and East elevations; Sheet 36 shows South and West elevations. Vision tool analysis of Sheet 35 confirmed that floor levels are clearly marked with elevations (Level 1 at 543.00, Level 2 at 563.66, Level 3 at 575.31, Level 4 at 586.97, Level 5 at 598.63, Level 6 at 610.28, Roof at 625.94). Architectural elements including windows with mullions, projecting balconies with railings, varied materials, recessed sections, projecting bays, varied rooflines/parapets, and ground-level features are all visible. Both sheets include Material Legend identifying five exterior finishes: Fiber Cement Board (Painted), King Brick, Wood Tone Fiber Cement, Glass, and Living Wall. The elevations are detailed color renderings with shading and texture showing architectural depth, not simple outlines.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires building elevations showing architectural elements when subject to Compatibility Standards. The elevations must be present and show sufficient detail to understand the building's architectural character. Sheets 35 and 36 provide comprehensive elevations for all four building faces with detailed architectural elements: fenestration patterns, balcony details, material variations, floor-to-floor heights, and building articulation. The material legends allow reviewers to understand the proposed exterior finishes. These are not simplified massing diagrams but detailed architectural renderings suitable for compatibility review. The elevations satisfy the completeness requirement by providing the necessary architectural detail for subsequent technical review against compatibility standards.
findings.explanation: Sheets 35 & 36 provide detailed building elevations for all four sides with architectural elements and material legends

findings.observation: Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 1 of 2) contains a 'COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINES' table in Block 3 (per blocks.md). Vision tool analysis confirmed the table shows distance-based building height restrictions: 0'-10' (screening zone with 0' allowable height), 10'-25' (restricted zone with 0' allowable height), 25'-50' (40' allowable height), and 50'-75' (60' allowable height). The vision tool also confirmed that setback lines are drawn and labeled on the site plan drawing itself, with labels reading '10' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE', '25' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE', '50' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE', and '75' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE'. These setback lines are most explicitly delineated running parallel to the southern property boundary adjacent to SF-3 zoned property. On the western edge adjacent to SF-3 zoning, a '75' BUILDING SETBACK PER REZONE' line is clearly marked. Adjacent SF-3 properties are shown to the west (Kinney Avenue Bungalows) and south (Lot A).
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires that setbacks adjacent to residential uses or zoning be shown on plans when subject to Compatibility Standards. Sheet 14 satisfies this requirement by providing both tabular and graphical representations of compatibility setbacks. The table quantifies the height restrictions at various distances from the property line, while the labeled setback lines on the plan drawing show exactly where these restrictions apply relative to the adjacent SF-3 residential zoning. The combination of the table and the drawn/labeled setback lines provides sufficient information for compatibility review. The setbacks are shown in relation to the actual adjacent residential zoning (SF-3 to west and south), meeting the requirement that setbacks adjacent to residential uses or zoning be depicted on the plans.
findings.explanation: Sheet 14 shows compatibility setback table with height restrictions and labeled setback lines (10', 25', 50', 75') adjacent to SF-3 residential zoning

summary: All 3 checklist items pass. Site is subject to Compatibility Standards (CS-V zoning within 75 ft of SF-3 residential). Required land use map (Sheet 13), building elevations (Sheets 35-36), and setback depictions (Sheet 14) are all present.
